title: Vertex-minor universality of a random graph
summary: Given a graph $G$ and a vertex $v\in V(G)$, a local complementation at $v$ on $G$ is an operation that replaces the induced graph on the neighborhood of $v$ by its complement. A graph $H$ is a vertex-minor if $H$ can be obtained from $G$ by a sequence of vertex deletions and local complementation. A graph is said to be $k$-vertex-minor universal if it contains every $k$-vertex graph on any $k$-subset of vertices as a vertex minor.
